chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of Maghrib, and he said: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم for every salat (prayer) with two times, except the salat (prayer) of Maghrib, for indeed its time is one, and its time is its becoming obligatory.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first two reports, because the way to reconcile them is that the time of Maghrib is restricted: there is not, between its beginning and its end, the same breadth as there is between the beginning of the time and its end in the rest of the prayers, as we shall clarify later. He did not mean that it has one single time such that it is not permissible for it to be advanced or delayed. And no one may say, in reconciling these reports, that Maghrib prayer is singled out from among the rest of the prayers, and say that every prayer has two times except Maghrib, because here there are detailed reports, which we have cited in our larger book, that include mention of Maghrib prayer and that it has two times, an earlier and a later one. Perhaps we may mention some of them later, if something arises that requires that. And when the matter is as such, this interpretation is not possible, and nothing besides what we have said is admissible.

key_terms.الْجَمْعِ بَيْنَهُمَا: reconciling the reports with one another
key_terms.بِوَقْتَيْنِ: with two designated times, an earlier and a later period
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib prayer specifically under discussion
key_terms.مُضَيَّقٌ: restricted or narrow in span compared to other prayer times
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the prescribed time of the Maghrib prayer
key_terms.وُجُوبُهَا: its becoming obligatory at the onset of its time

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith reconcile reports about whether Maghrib prayer has one time or two times?
ai.summary: This report discusses the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) and explains how narrations about its timing are to be reconciled. It states that Maghrib is more constrained than the other prayers, yet it should not be understood as having only one indivisible moment with no allowance for earlier and later bounds.
